scope: Twenty older revalidation cases whose cited claims come from one source and one physical-object record. No source claim, identity, or canonical value is changed.

entries.rationale: The American excavations at Seleucia claim describes archaeological context, while Seleucia, Iraq identifies the findspot. These are complementary facets of the same source report.
entries.review_basis: Explicit comparison of the two stored, source-attributed claims on one object record; compatibility does not independently verify the archaeological facts.

entries.rationale: About the 6th century CE and circa 6th century CE are equivalent qualified date descriptions from the same cited source.
entries.review_basis: Explicit comparison of the two stored, source-attributed claims on one object record; no canonical date is selected.

entries.rationale: Both descriptions report an opening diameter of 15 cm and depth of 5.6 cm; only order and punctuation differ.
entries.review_basis: Explicit comparison of the two stored, source-attributed claims on one object record; no value is deleted or averaged.

entries.rationale: Museo Sefardí de Toledo and Museo Sefardí de Toledo, Spain name the same institution; the second wording adds the country.
entries.review_basis: Explicit comparison of the two stored, source-attributed claims on one object record; this does not independently verify present custody.

entries.rationale: The sixth-to-eighth-century dating and Late-Post Sasanian period label are distinct chronological facets supplied by the same museum-derived source and can coexist.
entries.review_basis: Explicit comparison of stored source-attributed dating and period fields; compatibility does not independently establish the chronology.
